key_insight: PINNs reproduce the global evolution of turbulent, self-gravitating molecular clouds in 2D and 3D while showing weak training-cost dependence on spatial resolution.
engineering_relevance: This mesh-free approach offers a promising complement to grid-based simulation for computationally demanding, multiscale compressible flows with self-gravity.
method: Embed governing physics in the neural-network training objective.
Model isothermal clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulence.
Benchmark density and velocity predictions against Athena++ finite-volume simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate global evolution over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, subsonic and supersonic regimes, and dimensionalities, with training cost rising less than 25% from 128³ to 1024³.
watch_item: Global agreement and weak resolution-dependent training cost do not alone establish accuracy for shocks or small-scale structure, or an absolute speed advantage over Athena++.
paper_title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
